title: How NASA Filmed Perseverance Landing on Mars
description: Onboard cameras captured the Perseverance rover descending into Jezero Crater on February 18, 2021. This real footage shows the entire automated touchdown sequence from atmospheric entry to the surface.
hook_card: Seven minutes of terror on Mars.

shots.narration: This is real footage of a one-ton rover descending directly toward the red surface of Mars.
On February 18, 2021, the spacecraft entered the Martian atmosphere travelling at twenty thousand kilometres per hour.
Radio signals took eleven minutes to reach Earth, meaning the entire landing was over before mission control knew.
While still moving faster than sound, the craft deployed a twenty-one-point-five-metre parachute patterned with binary code.
Here, a rocket-powered descent stage hovers in place, lowering the rover on seven-point-six-metre cables.
With the rover safe, the descent stage cuts its tethers and flies away to crash at a distance.
Perseverance settled inside Jezero Crater, where a river delta and lake existed billions of years ago.
This marks the first time cameras on a landing craft recorded touchdown on another world.
